reports.title: Air Products Reports Fiscal 2026 Full-Year and Fourth Quarter Results; Provides Fiscal 2027 Guidance

guidance.heading: Guidance
section: •Fiscal 2027 full-year adjusted EPS guidance* of $14.15 to $14.50; fiscal 2027 first quarter adjusted EPS guidance* of $3.35 to $3.45
•Expect fiscal year 2027 capital expenditures* in the range of $3.0 billion to $3.5 billion
Fiscal 2026 Full-Year Consolidated Results (comparison versus prior year)

LEHIGH VALLEY, Pa. (November 5, 2026) - Air Products (NYSE:APD) today reported full-year fiscal 2026 GAAP results, including operating income of $23 million, operating margin of 0.2 percent, and EPS# of $2.39. This compares with an operating loss of $877 million, operating margin of negative 7.3 percent, and loss per share# of $1.74 in the prior year. Both periods reflect significant charges related to business and asset actions, primarily associated with previously announced project exit decisions. The non-GAAP financial measures discussed below exclude these charges, as well as other items, as described in the "Reconciliations of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" section of this release.
Fiscal 2026 full-year sales of $13.0 billion increased eight percent, or $954 million, on four percent higher volumes, two percent higher energy cost pass-through, and two percent favorable currency.

On a non-GAAP basis, fiscal 2026 full-year adjusted operating income* of $3.2 billion increased 11 percent over the prior year, primarily due to higher on-site volumes, favorable currency, and higher pricing. These benefits were partially offset by higher costs, driven by fixed-cost inflation and higher incentive compensation, partially offset by productivity improvements and lower depreciation. Adjusted operating margin* of 24.4 percent improved 70 basis points. Adjusted EPS* of $13.45 increased 12 percent over the prior year and also benefited from higher equity affiliates' income.
# Per share amounts are calculated and presented on a diluted basis from continuing operations attributable to Air Products.

desk.headline: Sales up 12% to $3.56bn, beat; adjusted EPS $3.61 in line; first fiscal 2027 outlook of $14.15–14.50 adjusted EPS
results: Quarterly sales rose 12% to $3.56bn on 9% higher volumes; adjusted EPS rose 6% to $3.61, just above the midpoint of the company's own range.
Volumes were lifted by a large one-off asset sale linked to an early contract termination in the Americas, where sales jumped 27%.
Adjusted operating margin slipped 1.5 points to 24.1% on higher costs; GAAP EPS of $2.62 includes a $0.91 charge, mainly on two China coal gasification plants.
Full fiscal 2026: sales up 8% to $13.0bn, adjusted EPS up 12% to $13.45; GAAP EPS was only $2.39 after $3.2bn of project-exit charges.
Capital spending fell $1.8bn to $3.3bn, operating cash flow rose to $4.7bn, and dividends of $1.6bn were paid.

guidance.summary: First outlook for fiscal 2027 (year to Sep 2027): adjusted EPS of $14.15–14.50, up 5–8%, and $3.35–3.45 for the December quarter. Capital spending is expected at $3.0–3.5bn.

points: The outlook assumes about 2% volume growth, with pricing and productivity expected to more than cover inflation and about $50m more from cost cuts.
Higher interest costs from cancelled projects and a tax rate rising to 19% are expected to be a 2% drag on FY27 earnings.
Helium faces a weaker first quarter on lower pricing after a contract renewal, plus a non-cash hit from an inventory accounting change.
The NEOM green ammonia plant is said to be essentially built, with no FY27 earnings impact and full running targeted for late 2027.
Over $2bn of electronics wins took the industrial gas backlog to $3.3bn; management expects to be cash-flow positive in FY27 and is weighing a 10–15% India IPO.
call.source: Call transcript — The Motley Fool, 5 Nov 2026; call summary — Yahoo Finance, 5 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Whether volumes grow without the one-off Americas asset sale that boosted this quarter.
Helium pricing in the December quarter and progress selling the remaining China gasification plant.
NEOM start-up timing and whether cash flow turns positive enough to restart buybacks.
